title: HTTP 1 connection leak
body:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/112.0

Steps to reproduce:

A site on my workplace intranet recently started leaking http1 connections.  Every time it's reloaded, the "active http <= 1.1" column in about:networking permanently ticks up by one.  Once it reaches 6 or 7, loading the site stalls forever until you close and reopen Firefox.
The browser first tries to load the page in http2, then receives an ntlm authentication prompt, and retries in http1.  While it loads, it also opens two http1 websocket connections.  Turning off http2 or blocking the websocket script prevents the issue.


Actual results:

This happens: https://profiler.firefox.com/public/mtf5f6rdgk88e3x74xjnafxbkzrybdh9a0wjshg/marker-table/?globalTrackOrder=01&thread=4&v=8

According to Mozregression, this started sometime on December 21-22.  I bisected the rest of the way by hand and I believe it began with bug 1774572.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Thanks to this [PR](https://github.com/firefox-devtools/profiler/pull/4973), I finally managed to extract the log from the profiler.

This is what happened:
1. We disable HTTP/2 for a transaction [here](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/7c573d9eb97e7b1ba383239bfac9260b26983544/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpConnectionMgr.cpp#1441) because the server doesn't support WebSocket over HTTP/2.
```
2024-05-29 01:22:58.948096435 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp GetH2orH3ActiveConn() request for ent 207ae65ce50 .S........[tlsflags0x00000000]qdevweb.skyward.com:443^partitionKey=%28https%2Cskyward.com%29 found an active but inexperienced connection 207b02c5c00 in native connection entry
2024-05-29 01:22:58.948097412 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp TryingDispatchTransaction: an active h2 connection exists
2024-05-29 01:22:58.948437011 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp Http2Session::GetWebSocketSupport 207af11c000 enable=1 allow=0 processed=1
2024-05-29 01:22:58.948437988 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp TryingDispatchTransaction: this is a websocket upgrade
2024-05-29 01:22:58.948438964 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp TryingDispatchTransaction: no support for websockets over Http2
```
2. We create a new HTTP/1.1 connection and connect to the server.
3. This server requires NTLM authentication, so we set the connection `sticky` and make the next transaction use the same connection.
4. We added this connection to another connection entry [here](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/7c573d9eb97e7b1ba383239bfac9260b26983544/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpConnectionMgr.cpp#1851). However, this entry differs from the one used in step 1 because [disabling HTTP/2 changes the hash key of the connection information](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/7c573d9eb97e7b1ba383239bfac9260b26983544/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpTransaction.cpp#2751). As a result, the same connection appears in the active connection lists of two different entries.
```
2024-05-29 01:22:57.372705078 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp nsHttpConnectionMgr::ProcessNewTransaction trans=207ac628800 sticky connection=207ae94c400
2024-05-29 01:22:57.372706298 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp nsHttpConnectionMgr::ProcessNewTransaction trans=207ac628800 sticky connection=207ae94c400 needs to go on the active list
2024-05-29 01:22:57.372707519 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp nsHttpConnectionMgr::ActivateTimeoutTick() this=207a377d100 mTimeoutTick=207ad1cee60
2024-05-29 01:22:57.372709472 UTC - [Parent Process 67808: Socket Thread]: D/nsHttp nsHttpConnectionMgr::DispatchTransaction [ent-ci=.S...X....[tlsflags0x00000000]qdevweb.skyward.com:443^partitionKey=%28https%2Cskyward.com%29 2079911a4c0 trans=207ac628800 caps=120a184 conn=207ae94c400 priority=0 isHttp2=0 isHttp3=0]
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Created attachment 9472682
Bug 1821878 - Ensure the fallback connection is in the right connection entry, r=#necko


When falling back from HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1, the newly created HTTP/1.1 connection was added to the original connection entry.
However, since HTTP/2 was disabled, the connection hash key had already changed. As a result, the same connection appeared in the active connection lists of two different entries.
This fix ensures that the new HTTP/1.1 connection is correctly placed in the appropriate connection entry.
